findings.description: The docblock says 'pup makes each [output] in a holder of its own', but the Python coverage output is `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'pup-coverage-'))` (src/adapters/python.adapter.ts:350), directly in the shared tmpdir with no holder; the property that matters (an ungranted parent) still holds, so only the comment is wrong.

Under `pup init`/`pup audit` the child's checkout is the operator's repo, so nothing may now write under `<repo>/.worktrees`. A TS repo whose vitest/jest config has no `include` discovers `.worktrees/sN/**` tests, and any that write beside themselves (new snapshots, fixtures, a default-include `tsc` emit) now fail with EPERM, turning a passing baseline stage into a recorded FAIL while sessions exist. This is worth naming in ADR 0117's ceilings rather than a break.

`writeProfile` now takes three positional `string[]` lists (writable, scratch, outputs), each with a different security treatment. Swapping the two trailing `[]`-defaulted arrays still typechecks but silently changes the profile. The first parameter is still named `writablePaths` although the body treats it as `pinnedCheckouts`, while `GateChildOptions.writablePaths` now flows into `outputPaths`. An options object `{ checkouts, scratch, outputs }` would name each role at the call site.

The unlink-deny rule builds its `(literal ...)` clauses with an inline map nested three templates deep, right beside the `subpaths` closure that does the same for `(subpath ...)`. It is the only place outside the helper that escapes inline. A sibling `literals` closure would make it read `(deny file-write-unlink${literals(...)}${subpaths(...)})`.

The test helper `profile()` grows to five positional `string[]` parameters, so call sites like `profile(['/repo'], [], [], ['/repo/a'], ['/repo/b'])` can't be read without counting commas, and a swap still typechecks. Taking a `Partial<{...}>` object, as `sandboxProfile` itself does, would name each list.

The new `vi.mock('node:fs', …)` wrapping `lstatSync` to fake another device goes beyond docs/conventions/testing.md §"When `vi.mock` is right", which reserves `vi.mock` for tmux and `claude -p` ("That is the whole current list"). Either extend that list with the reason (a real mount is out of reach in a test process) or stub without `vi.mock`.

The `gateInvocation` call-site comment ("the caller's are outputs a tool may remove and make again, so writeProfile refuses one that holds a .git or cannot be read") repeats the `writeProfile` JSDoc and decision 117. Keep at most the "(decision 117)" pointer.

The `writeProfile` JSDoc tail narrates the attack and the walk mechanics ("moved out, `.worktrees/s1` had its pointer file rewritten in scratch ... What the walk cannot see into is sealed whole"), which `nestedRepoPaths`'s doc and ADR 0117 already hold. It also mixes the grant, output and walk rules in one hard-to-scan block.
ADR 0117 lines 40-41 are one overlong line and lines 131-132 break mid-sentence oddly, while the rest of the ADR (like 0116) wraps at about 95 columns. Cosmetic only.
